newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians irked by government corruption -poll.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians irked by government corruption -poll.

text.p: Most Palestinians would support an initiative by Palestinian legislators to bring down the government of President Yasser Arafat over a recent corruption report, a poll showed on Monday.
The Centre for Palestine Research and Studies (CPRS) poll of 1,317 Palestinian showed Arafat's popularity had dropped by 11 points since April, but remained high at over 68 percent.
Support for the peace process with Israel had risen and most Palestinians favoured a return the bargaining table, according to the poll.

The CPRS poll was conducted earlier this month after an auditing office set up by Arafat concluded ministers and top civil servants had squandered or mismanaged $326 million in public funds last year.

Asked if they supported a "Palestinian Legislative Council vote of no-confidence in the Palestinian Cabinet" based on the findings of the auditing office, nearly 52 percent said yes compared with 31.5 percent who had said no. The rest had no opinion.
"More and more people are becoming sceptical about Palestinian handling of corruption. This is particularly true of young, educated males," said the centre's director of projects, Khalil Shikaki.

More than 68 percent of those questioned evaluated the "performance of the institution of the Presidency" as very good or good. Nearly 13 percent said it was fair and 9.3 percent said it was bad or very bad.
Support for the peace process rose eight points since April to 68, with 56 percent wanting to renew talks with Israel.

Israel-PLO negotiations halted in March when Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. Israel claims Jerusalem as its undivided capital. Palestinians want it as a capital of their future state.
The poll has a margin of error of three percent.
